message.content:
Here’s a list of the public holidays in Canada for 2023 that create long weekends (holidays falling on a Friday or Monday, or those that are observed on the nearest weekday if they fall on a weekend). These are the dates you’ll see as “long weekends” in most provinces:

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Observed (if applicable) | Notes |
|---------|-------------|---------------------------|-------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Jan 2 (Monday) | Observed on the following Monday |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Feb 20 (Monday) | — | Only in those provinces |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Fri‑Sat‑Sun) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 3 (Monday) | Observed on the following Monday |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| Thanksgiving (Canada) | Oct 9 (Monday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Monday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | — | Creates a long weekend (Sat‑Sun‑Mon) |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 (Tuesday) | — | Not a long weekend unless combined with Christmas |

These are the holidays that will give you a three‑day break (or longer if you combine them with adjacent weekends). If you need province‑specific holidays beyond the ones listed above, let me know which provinces you’re interested in and I can add those details.
